name: che-ical-mcp
description: Native EventKit integration for macOS Calendar and Reminders apps
long_description: A powerful MCP server providing 29 tools for managing macOS Calendar events and Reminders. Features include attendee/organizer read-only access, per-event timezone support, undo/redo, flexible date parsing, fuzzy calendar matching, batch operations with dry-run preview, advanced filtering/sorting/limiting, conflict detection, duplicate finding, multi-keyword search, recurring event occurrence-level operations, MCP-level #hashtag tags for reminders, and support for iCloud, Google, and Exchange calendars. Requires macOS 14.0 (Sonoma) or later.

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List all available calendars and reminder lists

tools.name: create_calendar
tools.description: Create a new calendar or reminder list (if saving a reminder list reports an error but the list was saved, the call succeeds and store_differs and note name any fields the store holds differently: store_differs lists their keys, from `title` and `account`, and creating it again with the same parameters may make a second copy); a title is 1 to 255 characters and not only whitespace, which does not promise that a long title stays, and type is event or reminder; not undoable: its undo is refused and the entry discarded, so the next undo reverts the operation recorded before it

tools.name: delete_calendar
tools.description: A failed deletion of a reminder list should change nothing (#459; not measured for a list). Delete a calendar or reminder list (this cannot be undone, with every event or reminder in it: its undo is refused and the entry discarded, so the next undo reverts the operation recorded before it); require_empty refuses a non-empty one, events checked only about 200 years either side of now (answer: checked_empty, searched_from, searched_to or reminders_found)

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List calendar events in a date range with optional detail_level, fields, display_timezone, filtering, sorting, and limiting (any range is searched in full, up to 146,000 days, about 400 years; over 1462 days, a read past about 200,000 occurrences (about 2,000 a year over 100 years) is refused, and without limit at most 500 events are returned, the first in the requested sort; truncated: true when fewer events are returned than event_count); reports item_timezone (the event's own time zone, null when floating) and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the start, negative = after)

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a new calendar event with optional reminders, recurrence, structured location, and per-event timezone (an all-day date whose offset moves it to another day in this Mac's zone is reported in warnings); unknown recurrence keys are refused

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update an existing calendar event (including timezone, recurrence span for recurring; the response's id is the identifier after the save, with id_changed and previous_id when a move to another account or a split of the series changed it, and occurrence_id for an edit of one occurrence; span all through an occurrence edited on its own is refused while an earlier occurrence remains, and with span all or future through it title, notes, location and recurrence can be written, dates and a few others only in the measured shapes the refusal lists, the rest writing nothing; span all through the series' id goes through its first occurrence when that one was edited on its own, with occurrence_id; occurrence_start for the occurrence occurrence_date matched; warnings for an all-day date whose offset moves the day) (annotated destructive: updates can replace or clear existing values; an update that touches a recurring event cannot be undone); unknown recurrence keys are refused, and so is a rule change on one occurrence (span this)

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete a calendar event (with occurrence support for recurring; span all through an occurrence edited on its own is refused while another occurrence remains, deleting nothing; span all through the series' id deletes from its first occurrence when that one was edited on its own, which cannot be undone, with occurrence_id and undo_note)

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.description: List reminders with structured recurrence rules, due-date precision, start date and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the due date, negative = after), and item_timezone (the reminder's own time zone, null when floating)

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.description: Create a new reminder with optional due date (a bare YYYY-MM-DD makes it date-only), recurrence, location trigger, relative alarms (alarms_minutes_offsets, minutes before a due date with a time; when the earliest alarm is off the due time, alarms_note says so: in the rows measured the Reminders.app list showed the earliest alarm time, not the due time, and the one notification checked showed it too) and tags (if the save reports an error but the reminder was saved, the call succeeds and store_differs and note name any fields the store holds differently: store_differs lists their keys, from `title`, `list`, `notes`, `priority`, `completion`, `url`, `start`, `due`, `due time zone`, `alarm count` and `recurrence rule count`, and creating it again with the same parameters may make a second copy); unknown recurrence keys are refused

tools.name: update_reminder
tools.description: Update an existing reminder, writing only the fields the call changes; a failed save changes nothing (#459) (including tags, clear_due_date, recurrence and clear_recurrence (a rule change does not move the due date; recurrence_note says when it is off the rule's days), alarms_minutes_offsets, which replaces only the relative alarms, with alarms_note when relative alarms are left on a reminder made date-only or undated, or, on a call that touches the alarms or the due date, when the earliest alarm is off the due time (in the rows measured the Reminders.app list showed the earliest alarm time, not the due time, and the one notification checked showed it too); changing due_date also moves the start date and absolute-date alarms, a bare YYYY-MM-DD due_date makes it date-only and removes absolute-date alarms, realign_to_due puts them onto the due date, date_sync reports whether they agree; the response's id is the identifier after the save, with id_changed and previous_id) (annotated destructive: updates can replace or clear existing values); unknown recurrence keys are refused

tools.name: complete_reminder
tools.description: Complete or reopen a reminder (a failed save should change nothing, #459; the rollover was not measured) with an explicit operation result and observed next occurrence with its relative alarms (alarms_minutes_offsets), plus a top-level alarms_note when one appeared on the read-back (annotated destructive: completing a recurring reminder consumes an occurrence irreversibly)

tools.name: delete_reminder
tools.description: Delete a reminder (a failed deletion should leave it as it was, #459; not measured for this tool)

tools.name: search_events
tools.description: Search events by keyword(s) with AND/OR matching, optional detail_level, fields, display_timezone, and limit (ranges up to 146,000 days, about 400 years; over 1462 days, a read past about 200,000 occurrences (about 2,000 a year over 100 years) is refused, and without limit at most 500 events are returned; any cut keeps those closest to today; truncated: true when fewer events are returned than event_count); reports item_timezone (the event's own time zone, null when floating) and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the start, negative = after)

tools.name: list_events_quick
tools.description: List events with quick time range shortcuts (today, tomorrow, this_week, etc.) with optional detail_level, fields, display_timezone, and limit; reports item_timezone (the event's own time zone, null when floating) and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the start, negative = after)

tools.name: create_events_batch
tools.description: Create multiple events at once (each result reports all-day dates whose offset moves the day in warnings); unknown recurrence keys fail that item

tools.name: check_conflicts
tools.description: Check for overlapping events in a time range with attendees/organizer (ranges up to 146,000 days, about 400 years; over 1462 days, a read past about 200,000 occurrences (about 2,000 a year over 100 years) is refused); reports item_timezone (the event's own time zone, null when floating) and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the start, negative = after)

tools.name: copy_event
tools.description: Copy an event (new identifier; recurrence and attendees not copied); with delete_original it moves the event like move_events_batch and refuses recurring events; without it, undo deletes the copy unless the copy was changed since

tools.name: move_events_batch
tools.description: Move events between calendars in place (keeps recurrence and attendees; the identifier can change, see id_changed); span this/all for recurring events; reports method and fields not carried over; recorded for undo

tools.name: delete_events_batch
tools.description: Delete multiple events at once; by event_ids, span all through an occurrence edited on its own is refused for that row while another occurrence remains; a date range with one bound searches 100 years out and reports searched_from/searched_to, and over a range wider than 1462 days (every one-sided range) more than 2000 deletions, or a read of more than about 200,000 occurrences (about 2,000 a year over 100 years), are refused, and span future does not retry occurrences an earlier deletion already removed with their series (by date range; by event_ids each row is looked up first, an occurrence's own id with span future deletes the later occurrences of its series and then refuses the call's undo, and the dry run marks a later row it reaches covered_by_earlier_row); otherwise one undo restores them (the undo is refused before any write, and its entry kept, when an event's calendar is missing or read-only, and discarding it then drops every event)

tools.name: find_duplicate_events
tools.description: Find duplicate events across calendars (ranges up to 146,000 days, about 400 years; over 1462 days, at most 2,000,000 comparisons and a read of about 200,000 occurrences (about 2,000 a year over 100 years)); calendar_names that match nothing, or fewer than two calendars, are refused

tools.name: update_calendar
tools.description: A rename or recolor of a reminder list writes only the field it changes, and a failed one should change nothing (#459; not measured for a list). Update a calendar's properties (rename or change color) (annotated destructive: updates can replace or clear existing values); a title is 1 to 255 characters and not only whitespace, which does not promise that a long title stays; not undoable: its undo is refused and the entry discarded, so the next undo reverts the operation recorded before it

tools.name: search_reminders
tools.description: Search reminders by keyword(s) or tag with AND/OR matching, structured recurrence metadata, start date and time-based alarms (minutes_before: positive = before the due date, negative = after), and item_timezone (the reminder's own time zone, null when floating)

tools.name: create_reminders_batch
tools.description: Create multiple reminders at once (with tags and per-row alarms_minutes_offsets; when the earliest alarm is off the due time, the row's alarms_note says so: in the rows measured the Reminders.app list showed the earliest alarm time, not the due time, and the one notification checked showed it too; a bare YYYY-MM-DD due_date makes a date-only reminder; a result may carry store_differs and note, as create_reminder does, and creating that reminder again with the same parameters may make a second copy); a row with an unknown key fails, and recurrence and location_trigger need create_reminder

tools.name: delete_reminders_batch
tools.description: Delete multiple reminders at once (a row that fails with a code stays as it was, #459; a busy pool refuses the call before any row is deleted, and a later row whose new store sees no data answers write_store_busy; one undo recreates them from the undo snapshot; the undo is refused before any write, and its entry kept, when a reminder's list is missing or read-only, and discarding it then drops every reminder)

tools.name: list_reminder_tags
tools.description: List all unique tags used across reminders with usage counts

tools.name: cleanup_completed_reminders
tools.description: Delete all completed reminders in one call (dry_run=true by default; a row that fails with a code stays as it was, #459; a busy pool refuses the call before any row is deleted, and a later row whose new store sees no data answers write_store_busy). Optional calendar_name / calendar_source to scope to a single list. Each call is one undo entry and clears the redo history; one undo recreates the deleted reminders, one at a time, from the undo snapshot; the undo is refused before any write, and its entry kept, when a reminder's list is missing or read-only, and discarding it then drops every reminder.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent recorded operation (create_calendar, update_calendar and delete_calendar are recorded but never undone: their undo is refused and the entry discarded, so the next undo reverts the operation recorded before it; refused without writing when the item was changed since; the record stays until the change is reverted or the user discards it; for the undo of an update of a one-off event or a reminder, called with keep_later_edits (ask the user first), it restores only what the update changed and keeps later edits elsewhere, and refuses as before when a later edit is in what the update changed; a series created here whose first occurrence was deleted later is refused until the user discards it; also refused when a reminder's recorded list is not found, and discarding a delete_reminder undo loses the deleted reminder; likewise when an event's recorded calendar is not found, and discarding a delete_event undo loses the deleted event; a batch undo is refused before any write, its entry kept, when an item's calendar or list is missing or read-only, and discarding it drops every item of the batch; called with restore_available (ask the user first), such a batch undo instead restores the items whose calendar or list is in place and keeps an entry of only the others under the same id; a batch undo that fails part-way keeps only the items not yet restored; a batch undo names the first five restored reminders whose store holds fields differently, then how many more, also when it stops part-way; updates to recurring events are never undone; a delete of an occurrence and the following ones is undone only when it started at the series' first occurrence and removed it all, and a batch holding one that did not is refused before any write and its entry discarded; a deleted occurrence comes back as a one-off event; a series deleted whole comes back from its rules with its exceptions inside the checked window (at most four years, around the time of the delete; for a count, also the four years from its first occurrence) restored: an occurrence deleted on its own earlier stays deleted, one edited on its own comes back as a separate one-off event; exceptions outside that window, a first occurrence edited or deleted on its own, and a record that does not match the recreated series come back from the rules alone, while an edited occurrence moved more than a year outside the window is not restored and its slot counts as deleted, and undoing the earlier delete of an occurrence whose slot the restored series already holds (matched by series and original slot, not by title) writes nothing and says so; when a delete_reminder undo recreates a reminder the store then holds differently, the message names the fields), or explicitly discard the current top history record using discard_id from undo_history

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone operation (only completions are written again; for any other record redo writes nothing, answers success: false with the tool to use, and that entry is removed from the redo history; redo does not replay a create, delete, update or move by design; a completion redo is refused when the reminder changed since the undo)

tools.name: undo_history
tools.description: List undoable operations with stable record IDs, timestamps and undo/redo counts
